texts: We use comparisons when we want to state similarities or differences about people / places / objects / matters etc.
Adjectives are used in this topic but they take a new form. Check the following examples.
Statements
Questions
Negative statements
Joe is more attractive than Kalvin
Is Joe more attractive than Kalvin?
Joe is not more attractive than Kalvin.
China is bigger than Japan.
Is China bigger than Japan?
China is not bigger than Japan.
Computers are more useful than TVs.
Are computers more useful than TVs?
Computers are not more useful than TVs.

texts: TO CONSIDER
1. Adjectives can be divided into two groups: / Short (1 or 2 syllables) / Long (2 or more syllables).
2. Short adjectives take the –er + than particles: Joe is taller than Jim.
3.Long adjectives take the more + than particles: It is more expensive here than there.
4.Short adjectives that finish in –y change to I + er: She is prettier than you.
5. There are irregular adjectives: Good – Better than / Bad – Worse than.
6. We use the particles ‘as / as’ to state similarities: Joe is as tall as Jake.
7. There are adjectives who do not receive comparison degrees; those adjective have absolute meaning: This is the final test / Those people are dead.
8. Less + Adjective + than is used to state inferiority between two nouns. E.G. Alex is less determined than his brother.
9. There are three levels of comparison: Superiority , Equality and Inferiority

texts: Language Targets
Aspects
Examples
State superiority
He seems to be more interesting than his brother.
Express Equality
These cars are as expensive as that truck.
Establish inferiority
Your bag is less classy than mine.
Make general comparisons

Both brothers are very alike.
They don’t look the same to me.
Comparisons can deal with different aspects. they can also be used at any tense.
TO CONSIDER
*This is a bigger city.
*If you know the context,  the comparison can be used without mentioning the other person /object / place / matter etc.

texts: B. Listen to two tourist talking about some places they have visited.
Which are these places? What are they saying? Tell your teacher.
C. Read the following paragraph and identify where the comparisons are. After that, Answer the questions next to it. Finally, read it aloud with your teacher.
Brothers

Frank is taller than his brother Jake, but Jake is older than Frank. Both are good students, but Jake is a better runner. Frank is more interested in chess and reading; However, Jake is a better fan of sports and technology. Both speak two languages, though Frank has better French than Jake. Both of them love cars, but Jake is more into F1 races than Frank. They both are in the same school.
Who is taller?
Is Frank older than Jake?
Which brother is a better runner?
Is Jake more interested in chess and reading?
Is Frank more interested in sports and technology?
Who speaks two languages?.
Who has better French?.
What do they love?
